text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.2% today, continuing a steep two-week decline of 11% that began right after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th. The stock has lost ground steadily since that report, suggesting investors reacted negatively to the financial results or outlook—though the specific earnings details aren't summarized here. Crude oil prices remain relatively stable (US oil at $99.64/barrel), so the drop appears driven by company-specific factors rather than a broad energy sector collapse.

The timing matters: the earnings report dropped the same day geopolitical news about failed Iran negotiations surfaced, and U.S. political uncertainty over government funding and debt limits has emerged this week. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, unresolved Middle East tensions and domestic political gridlock can create unpredictability around both oil supply and regulatory costs, even if current oil prices haven't collapsed yet.
